accuracy.evidence: Every plural was checked against the Oxford Learner's Dictionaries entries and the Cambridge Grammar of English section on irregular plurals: vowel-change plurals foot/feet, tooth/teeth, goose/geese, man/men, woman/women, mouse/mice; -en plurals child/children, ox/oxen; zero plurals sheep and deer. Standards were checked against CCSS L.2.1b (frequently occurring irregular plurals: feet, children, teeth, mice, fish) and L.2.1a (collective nouns), and the National Curriculum in England Appendix 1 Years 1–2 for the regular -s/-es suffix. 'Adult humans have 32 teeth' (m7) matches the NHS adult dentition figure. Collective nouns used (flock of birds/sheep, pack of wolves/dogs, herd of cows, swarm of bees) are the standard ones.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors for this stage: over-regularisation (mouses, tooths, childs, sheeps, foots in the slip step; prediction 'mouses', 'gooses', 'sheeps'; challenge key 's'), double marking (feets, childrens, womens, geeses, mices; challenge key 'twice', p3, m1, m9), zero plurals treated as regular (deers, dears; challenge 'same', m4) and mixed-up collective nouns (a pack of birds; group step feedback, challenge 'flock' and 'pack', m8).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagirrpl is about how an irregular noun builds its plural: a test that rejects plain s for mouse, tooth and child, a dashed box over the vowel letters that only accepts the right replacement (oo→ee, a→e, ouse→ice), a three-family sort (change inside, add en, no change) and a collective-noun gap with a drawn crowd of animals. flagplural only adds -s or -es by the final letters; no other lab edits a word's interior. The lab_distinct gate passed under the 30% limit against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds out the rule by trying it: dragging mouse to 'Just add s' is refused with 'mouses is a slip', dropping e into foot gives 'fet is not right... listen to the middle sound', and sheep refused in 'Changes inside' is answered with 'It does not change at all'. Each completion line restates what was learned ('The middle changes and there is no s on the end').

predictions.evidence: Three predictions offer the tempting over-regularised form: 'mouses' (step 1, disproved when mouse only fits 'The word changes'), 'gooses' (step 2, disproved when only ee fits the dashed box, giving geese) and 'sheeps' (step 3, disproved when sheep only fits 'Stays the same').

challenge_feedback.evidence: Every wrong challenge choice is keyed to its slip: 's' for adding the regular suffix to an irregular noun (childs, foots, womans, gooses), 'twice' for adding s to an already plural form (childrens, feets, womens, geeses), 'same' for deers and dears, and 'flock' and 'pack' for wrong collective nouns. Six questions rotate so a retry gives a new item.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and the one ..., two ... pattern children say aloud, introducing regular, irregular, the three families and the two slips one per paragraph; the family readability limit passed in validate_lessons. Lab prompts are short ('Line 1 of 5: one plural is wrong. Tap it.'). The adult text uses the precise terms singular, plural, irregular plural, suffix, zero plural, collective noun.

no_filler.evidence: Every sentence teaches a form or a trap; the content gate found no banned phrases and explanation overlap with Regular Plural Nouns and every other lesson is under 12%. Feedback lines are specific to the word, for example 'child adds ren, not s: children.' and 'That word is already plural. Do not add s as well.'

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for all 6 steps: noun cards are about 170 px wide, the three family bins fit across 390 px with their labels, the vowel tiles and the three replacement tiles are large targets, the sentence tiles fit one line, and the step 2 heading was shortened after it clipped. The bird, cow and wolf crowd colours were lightened in dark mode after the first screenshots.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate completed every task with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Each drag has a labelled button equivalent ('cat: just add s', 'foot: put ee in the middle', 'a flock of birds'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback message.

sources: Common Core State Standards ELA L.2.1a (collective nouns) and L.2.1b (form and use frequently occurring irregular plural nouns: feet, children, teeth, mice, fish)
National Curriculum in England: English Appendix 1 Spelling, Years 1 and 2 (plural suffixes -s and -es)
Cambridge Grammar of English (Carter and McCarthy): irregular plurals by vowel change, -en and zero plural
